% Built from docs/paper/index.md by docs/paper/arxiv/build.py; do not edit by hand.
% Converter: pandoc $converter$
\documentclass[11pt,letterpaper]{article}

% Reproducible output: no trailer ID, no pdfTeX file information; the dates come from
% SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (build.py sets it with FORCE_SOURCE_DATE=1).
\pdftrailerid{}
\pdfsuppressptexinfo=-1
\tracinglostchars=2

\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage{textcomp}
\usepackage[letterpaper,margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage[protrusion=true,expansion=true]{microtype}
\DisableLigatures{encoding = *, family = tt*}

% The non-ASCII characters of index.md that pandoc leaves in main.tex. LaTeX maps the accented
% letters, the en dash and the section sign itself; build.py fails on any other character
% that is not listed here. The superscripts share one form, so "10⁻¹⁵" sets evenly.
\usepackage{newunicodechar}
\newunicodechar{−}{\textminus}
\newunicodechar{≤}{\ensuremath{\leq}}
\newunicodechar{×}{\texttimes}
\newunicodechar{÷}{\textdiv}
\newunicodechar{ψ}{\ensuremath{\psi}}
\newunicodechar{·}{\textperiodcentered}
\newunicodechar{…}{\textellipsis}
\newunicodechar{¹}{\textsuperscript{1}}
\newunicodechar{⁵}{\textsuperscript{5}}
\newunicodechar{⁹}{\textsuperscript{9}}
\newunicodechar{⁻}{\textsuperscript{\textminus}}

\usepackage{etoolbox}
\usepackage{graphicx}
% Recent versions of pdftex.def add a transparency /Group to every included PDF, which pdfTeX
% already copies from cairo's page, so the figure XObjects would carry the key twice. This
% switches the addition off, as older drivers, which have no such switch, never make it.
\makeatletter
\ifdefined\Gread@transgrouptrue\let\Gread@transgrouptrue\Gread@transgroupfalse\fi
\makeatother
\usepackage{xcolor}
\definecolor{linkblue}{rgb}{0.05,0.20,0.55}
\usepackage{array}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\usepackage{longtable}
\usepackage{caption}
\usepackage{needspace}
\usepackage{enumitem}
\usepackage{flafter}
\usepackage{placeins}
\usepackage{fvextra}
\usepackage{upquote}
\usepackage{tcolorbox}
\tcbuselibrary{breakable}
\usepackage{titlesec}
\usepackage{xurl}
% xurl lets a URL break anywhere; breaking after a separator is far cheaper than inside a word.
\makeatletter
\def\UrlBigBreaks{\do\/\do\.\do\-\do\_\do\:\do\=\do\&\do\?\do\#\do\,\do\;}
\makeatother
\mathchardef\UrlBigBreakPenalty=100
\mathchardef\UrlBreakPenalty=4000
\usepackage{hyperref}
\hypersetup{
  colorlinks=true,
  linkcolor=linkblue,
  citecolor=linkblue,
  urlcolor=linkblue,
  filecolor=linkblue,
  bookmarksnumbered=true,
  pdftitle={$title-meta$},
  pdfauthor={$author-meta$}
}

% Headings read as in index.md: "1. Introduction", "5.1 ...", "Appendix A. ..."; set ragged
% right, so that a two-line heading keeps its natural spaces.
\titleformat{\section}{\normalfont\Large\bfseries\filright}{\thesection.}{0.5em}{}
\titleformat{\subsection}{\normalfont\large\bfseries\filright}{\thesubsection}{0.5em}{}
\appto\appendix{%
  \titleformat{\section}{\normalfont\Large\bfseries\filright}{\appendixname~\thesection.}{0.5em}{}}

% Captions: the "Table X." and "Figure X." labels are part of the text, so LaTeX adds none.
\captionsetup{font=small,labelformat=empty,labelsep=none,justification=justified,
  singlelinecheck=false,skip=5pt}
\captionsetup[table]{position=top}
\setlength{\LTcapwidth}{\textwidth}
\setlength{\LTpre}{9pt plus 2pt}
\setlength{\LTpost}{9pt plus 2pt}
\newcolumntype{P}[1]{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash\hspace{0pt}}p{#1}}
\newcolumntype{R}[1]{>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash\hspace{0pt}}p{#1}}

% Inline code: break points after a separator, every 8 characters of a long hex string,
% (much costlier) after "_" or "-" inside a name, and, only when nothing else fits, after a
% "-" inside a command-line flag; spaces stretch a little (a typewriter space does not), so
% that a line holding mostly code can still be justified.
\newcommand{\codebrk}{\penalty50\relax}
\newcommand{\codebrkh}{\penalty100\relax}
\newcommand{\codebrkx}{\penalty500\relax}
\newcommand{\codebrkf}{\penalty2000\relax}
\newcommand{\codesp}{\hskip 0.5em plus 0.25em minus 0.1em\relax}

% Code blocks at \scriptsize: a framed line holds 109 characters, so the prompts keep their
% own line breaks.
\fvset{fontsize=\scriptsize,frame=single,framerule=0.4pt,rulecolor=\color{black!35},
  framesep=1.5mm,samepage=true,breaklines=true,
  breaksymbolleft={\tiny\ensuremath{\hookrightarrow}},breakaftersymbolpre={}}

\newtcolorbox{readerbox}[1]{breakable,title={#1},fonttitle=\bfseries\small,fontupper=\small,
  colback=linkblue!3,colframe=linkblue!55,colbacktitle=linkblue!12,coltitle=black,
  boxrule=0.5pt,arc=1pt,left=6pt,right=6pt,top=4pt,bottom=4pt,before skip=10pt,after skip=10pt}

% Floats stay near their first mention; a paragraph with long code may stretch rather than
% overflow.
\renewcommand{\topfraction}{0.85}
\renewcommand{\bottomfraction}{0.6}
\renewcommand{\textfraction}{0.12}
\renewcommand{\floatpagefraction}{0.75}
\makeatletter
\setlength{\@fptop}{0pt}
\makeatother
\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
\brokenpenalty=10000 % no word hyphenated across a page break

\providecommand{\tightlist}{%
  \setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}}
\setlist[itemize]{topsep=4pt}

\title{$title-tex$}
\author{$author$\\[2pt]\url{$repo-url$}}
\date{$date$}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
$abstract$
\end{abstract}

$body$
